scope: Named bone markings and structural spaces in supplied OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e chapters 6-8, plus named bony extensions found in whole-book text and confirmed figure-only labels.

entries.name: Articular cartilage
entries.description: Hyaline cartilage covers the epiphyseal surfaces that meet other bones, reducing friction and absorbing load.
reviewNotes: Cartilage tissue, not mineralized bone; preserve tissue context.

entries.name: Canaliculi
entries.description: Microscopic channels in the bone matrix connect osteocyte lacunae with one another and the central canal.
reviewNotes: Bone histology inset, not a macroscopic pin on the adult skeleton; distinguish bone central canal from spinal-cord central canal.
Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Central canal
entries.description: The longitudinal channel at the center of a compact-bone osteon contains vessels and nerves; it is not the central canal of the spinal cord.
reviewNotes: Bone histology inset, not a macroscopic pin on the adult skeleton; distinguish bone central canal from spinal-cord central canal.
Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Compact bone
entries.description: Dense osseous tissue forms the wall of a long-bone diaphysis and the outer layers of other bones.

entries.name: Concentric lamellae
entries.description: Concentric layers of mineralized matrix surround the central canal of an osteon.
reviewNotes: Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Diaphysis
entries.description: Tubular shaft that runs between the proximal and distal ends of a long bone.

entries.name: Diploe
entries.description: The spongy-bone layer lies between the outer and inner compact-bone layers of a flat skull bone.

entries.name: Endosteum
entries.description: A delicate membrane lines the medullary cavity and internal bone surfaces.
reviewNotes: Connective-tissue lining, not a surface opening on the adult skeleton.

entries.name: Epiphyseal line
entries.description: Completely ossified remnant of the epiphyseal plate.

entries.name: Epiphyseal plate
entries.description: (also, growth plate) sheet of hyaline cartilage in the metaphysis of an immature bone; replaced by bone tissue as the organ grows in length.

entries.name: Epiphysis
entries.description: Wide section at each end of a long bone; filled with spongy bone and red marrow.

entries.name: Lacunae
entries.description: Small spaces in mineralized bone matrix house osteocytes.
reviewNotes: Bone histology inset, not a macroscopic pin on the adult skeleton; distinguish bone central canal from spinal-cord central canal.
Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Medullary cavity
entries.description: Hollow region of the diaphysis; filled with yellow marrow.

entries.name: Metaphysis
entries.description: The transition between each epiphysis and the diaphysis contains the growth plate in an immature long bone.

entries.name: Nutrient foramen
entries.description: Small opening in the middle of the external surface of the diaphysis, through which an artery enters the bone to provide nourishment.

entries.name: Osteon
entries.description: The structural unit of compact bone consists of concentric lamellae surrounding a central canal.
reviewNotes: Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Perforating canal
entries.description: A transverse or oblique channel connects osteon central canals with vessels and nerves toward the periosteum and endosteum.
reviewNotes: Bone histology inset, not a macroscopic pin on the adult skeleton; distinguish bone central canal from spinal-cord central canal.
Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Periosteum
entries.description: A fibrous membrane covers the external bone surface except at articular-cartilage surfaces.
reviewNotes: Connective-tissue covering, not mineralized bone; show in a section or tissue layer.

entries.name: Spongy bone
entries.description: Trabecular osseous tissue occupies the interior of epiphyses and flat bones, with spaces that may contain marrow.

entries.name: Trabeculae
entries.description: The lattice-like plates and struts of spongy bone support loads while leaving spaces for marrow.
reviewNotes: Microscopic feature; requires a bone-section/histology illustration rather than an adult surface pin.

entries.name: Sigmoid sulcus of temporal bone
aliases: sigmoid sulcus of the temporal bones
entries.description: A groove on the inner temporal bone accommodates the sigmoid venous sinus; Table 6.2 uses it as the example of a sulcus.

sources.term: sigmoid sulcus of the temporal bones

entries.name: Temporal lines of parietal bone
aliases: temporal lines of the parietal bones
entries.description: Slight elongated ridges on the lateral skull are the named example of a line in Table 6.2.

sources.term: temporal lines of the parietal bones

entries.name: Auricular fissure
entries.description: Table 6.2 uses the historical expression auricular fissure as its fissure example. Current terminology names a tympanomastoid fissure of the temporal bone; the textbook supplies no labeled figure or precise target for this example.
reviewNotes: Historical anatomy explicitly equates tympano-mastoid and auricular fissure. FIPAT TA2 item 720 uses tympanomastoid fissure. Preserve the source wording in a terminology note and use an independently verified named fissure for identification practice.
Do not substitute the superior orbital fissure or petrotympanic fissure.

externalSources.title: FIPAT Terminologia Anatomica 2, Part II, item 720
Anatomy. A manual for students and practitioners, p43 (historical terminology)

entries.name: Canal
entries.description: A passage through bone; distinguish macroscopic canals from bone histology canals.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Condyle
entries.description: A rounded articular surface, as at an occipital condyle or distal femur.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Crest
entries.description: A prominent ridge, as at the iliac crest.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Facet
entries.description: A small, relatively flat articular surface; use a named vertebral facet as the example.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Fissure
entries.description: A narrow slit or cleft through or between bony parts.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Foramen
entries.description: An opening through bone; the plural is foramina.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Fossa
entries.description: A basin-like depression on a bone.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Fovea
entries.description: A small pit, as at the fovea capitis of the femur.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Head
entries.description: A prominent rounded articular surface, as at the proximal femur.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Line
entries.description: A slight elongated ridge, as at a parietal temporal line.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Meatus
entries.description: A passage or opening into a canal, as at the external acoustic meatus.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Process
entries.description: A projection from a bone, as at a vertebral transverse process.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Protuberance
entries.description: A bony projection or prominence, as at the chin.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Sinus
entries.description: An air-containing space within a skull bone in this skeletal context; a venous sinus is a different structure.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Spine
entries.description: A sharp or prominent process, as at the ischial spine.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Sulcus
entries.description: A groove, as at the temporal sigmoid sulcus.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Tubercle
entries.description: A small rounded bony projection.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Tuberosity
entries.description: A roughened bony prominence, as at the deltoid attachment on the humerus.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Alveolar process of mandible
entries.description: Upper border of mandibular body that contains the lower teeth.

entries.name: Alveolar process of maxilla
entries.description: Curved, inferior margin of the maxilla that supports and anchors the upper teeth.

entries.name: Alveolus
entries.description: A tooth is anchored within a deep bony socket of the alveolar process.
reviewNotes: Bony socket is included; the tooth itself is not a bone.

entries.name: Angle of mandible
entries.description: Rounded corner located at outside margin of the body and ramus junction.

entries.name: Anterior cranial fossa
entries.description: Shallowest and most anterior cranial fossa of the cranial base that extends from the frontal bone to the lesser wing of the sphenoid bone.

entries.name: Anterior fontanelle
entries.description: An infant skull fibrous gap between the adjacent developing bones; locate it on a newborn specimen, not as a hole in an adult skull.
reviewNotes: Developmental feature; use the newborn-skull illustration.

entries.name: Articular tubercle
entries.description: A smooth temporal-bone ridge immediately anterior to the mandibular fossa contributes to the temporomandibular joint.

entries.name: Body of mandible
entries.description: The U-shaped horizontal mandibular portion supports the lower teeth and meets the vertical ramus on each side.

entries.name: Body of sphenoid
entries.description: The central portion of the sphenoid supports the sella turcica superiorly and contains the sphenoid sinus.

entries.name: Calvaria
entries.description: The rounded skullcap forms the superior covering of the cranial cavity.

entries.name: Carotid canal
entries.description: Zig-zag tunnel providing passage through the base of the skull for the internal carotid artery to the brain; begins anteromedial to the styloid process and terminates in the middle cranial cavity, near the posterior-lateral base of the sella turcica.

entries.name: Condylar process of mandible
entries.description: The posterior upward projection from the mandibular ramus supports the mandibular condyle at its top; the whole process is larger than the articular condyle.

existingTarget.name: Mandibular condyles
existingTarget.relationship: related; whole process is larger than its articular condyle

entries.name: Coronal suture
entries.description: Joint that unites the frontal bone to the right and left parietal bones across the top of the skull.

entries.name: Coronoid process of mandible
entries.description: Flattened upward projection from the anterior margin of the mandibular ramus.

entries.name: Cranial base
entries.description: The complex floor of the brain case is divided into anterior, middle and posterior cranial fossae.
entries.pattern: Frontal bone||Ethmoid bone||Sphenoid bone||Temporal bone||Occipital bone

entries.name: Cranial cavity
entries.description: Interior space of the skull that houses the brain.
entries.pattern: Frontal bone||Parietal bone||Temporal bone||Occipital bone||Sphenoid bone||Ethmoid bone

entries.name: Cribriform plate
entries.description: Small, flattened areas with numerous small openings, located to either side of the midline in the floor of the anterior cranial fossa; formed by the ethmoid bone.

entries.name: Crista galli
entries.description: Small upward projection located at the midline in the floor of the anterior cranial fossa; formed by the ethmoid bone.

entries.name: Ethmoid air cells
entries.description: One of several small, air-filled spaces located within the lateral sides of the ethmoid bone, between the orbit and upper nasal cavity.

existingTarget.name: Ethmoidal air cells and sinus openings

entries.name: External acoustic meatus
entries.description: The ear-canal opening on the lateral temporal bone leads toward the tympanic membrane.

entries.name: External occipital protuberance
entries.description: Small bump located at the midline on the posterior skull.

entries.name: Foramen lacerum
entries.description: A ragged gap at the sphenoid-temporal-occipital junction is filled with cartilage in life; the internal carotid artery passes above it after leaving its canal.

entries.name: Foramen magnum
entries.description: Large opening in the occipital bone of the skull through which the spinal cord emerges and the vertebral arteries enter the cranium.

entries.name: Foramen ovale of the middle cranial fossa
entries.description: Oval- shaped opening in the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

sources.term: foramen ovale of the middle cranial fossa

entries.name: Foramen rotundum
entries.description: Round opening in the floor of the middle cranial fossa, located between the superior orbital fissure and foramen ovale.

entries.name: Foramen spinosum
entries.description: Small opening in the floor of the middle cranial fossa, located lateral to the foramen ovale.

entries.name: Fossa for lacrimal sac
entries.description: The depression at the anterior medial orbit houses the lacrimal sac and leads inferiorly into the nasolacrimal canal; this is not the frontal-bone fossa for the lacrimal gland.

entries.name: Frontal sinus
entries.description: Air-filled space within the frontal bone; most anterior of the paranasal sinuses.

entries.name: Glabella
entries.description: Slight depression of frontal bone, located at the midline between the eyebrows.

entries.name: Greater wings of sphenoid
entries.description: Lateral projections of the sphenoid bone that form the anterior wall of the middle cranial fossa and an area of the lateral skull.

entries.name: Hard palate
entries.description: Bony structure that forms the roof of the mouth and floor of the nasal cavity, formed by the palatine process of the maxillary bones and the horizontal plate of the palatine bones.

entries.name: Horizontal plate of palatine bone
entries.description: Medial extension from the palatine bone that forms the posterior quarter of the hard palate.

entries.name: Hypoglossal canal
entries.description: Paired openings that pass anteriorly from the anterior-lateral margins of the foramen magnum deep to the occipital condyles.

entries.name: Hypophyseal fossa
entries.description: The rounded depression in the floor of the sella turcica houses the pituitary gland.

existingTarget.name: Sella turcica
existingTarget.relationship: related; fossa lies within the larger saddle-shaped sella

entries.name: Inferior orbital fissure
entries.description: The opening along the inferior-lateral posterior orbit is shown separately from the superior orbital fissure.

externalSources.title: Anatomy of the Inferior Orbital Fissure: Implications for Endoscopic Cranial Base Surgery (cadaveric anatomical study)
externalSources.purpose: Contributing bone boundary cross-check, including small palatine contribution

entries.name: Infraorbital foramen
entries.description: Opening located on anterior skull, below the orbit.

entries.name: Infratemporal fossa
entries.description: Space on lateral side of skull, below the level of the zygomatic arch and deep (medial) to the ramus of the mandible.

entries.name: Internal acoustic meatus
entries.description: Opening into petrous ridge, located on the lateral wall of the posterior cranial fossa.

entries.name: Jugular foramen
entries.description: Irregularly shaped opening located in the lateral floor of the posterior cranial cavity.

entries.name: Lambdoid suture
entries.description: The posterior skull suture joins the occipital bone with the right and left parietal bones.

entries.name: Lateral pterygoid plate
entries.description: Paired, flattened bony projections of the sphenoid bone located on the inferior skull, lateral to the medial pterygoid plate.

entries.name: Lesser wings of sphenoid
aliases: lesser wings of the sphenoid bone
entries.description: Lateral extensions of the sphenoid bone that form the bony lip separating the anterior and middle cranial fossae.

sources.term: lesser wings of the sphenoid bone

entries.name: Lingula
entries.description: Small flap of bone located on the inner (medial) surface of mandibular ramus, next to the mandibular foramen.

entries.name: Mandibular condyle
entries.description: The oval articular head at the top of the condylar process articulates with the temporal bone.

entries.name: Mandibular foramina
entries.description: Opening located on the inner (medial) surface of the mandibular ramus.

entries.name: Mandibular fossa
entries.description: Oval depression located on the inferior surface of the skull.

entries.name: Mandibular notch
entries.description: Large U-shaped notch located between the condylar process and coronoid process of the mandible.

entries.name: Mastoid fontanelle
entries.description: An infant skull fibrous gap between the adjacent developing bones; locate it on a newborn specimen, not as a hole in an adult skull.
reviewNotes: Developmental feature; use the newborn-skull illustration.

entries.name: Mastoid portion of temporal bone
entries.description: The posterior temporal region gives rise to the inferiorly projecting mastoid process.

entries.name: Mastoid process
entries.description: Large bony prominence on the inferior, lateral skull, just behind the earlobe.

entries.name: Maxillary sinus
entries.description: Air-filled space located with each maxillary bone; largest of the paranasal sinuses.

entries.name: Medial pterygoid plate
entries.description: Paired, flattened bony projections of the sphenoid bone located on the inferior skull medial to the lateral pterygoid plate; form the posterior portion of the nasal cavity lateral wall.

entries.name: Mental foramen
entries.description: Opening located on the anterior- lateral side of the mandibular body.

entries.name: Mental protuberance
entries.description: Inferior margin of anterior mandible that forms the chin.

entries.name: Middle cranial fossa
entries.description: Centrally located cranial fossa that extends from the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone to the petrous ridge.

entries.name: Middle nasal concha
entries.description: Nasal concha formed by the ethmoid bone that is located between the superior and inferior conchae.

existingTarget.name: Superior and middle nasal conchae
existingTarget.relationship: grouped target; superior and middle conchae remain distinct

entries.name: Mylohyoid line
entries.description: Bony ridge located along the inner (medial) surface of the mandibular body.

entries.name: Nasal cavity
entries.description: Opening through skull for passage of air.
entries.pattern: Nasal bone||Frontal bone||Ethmoid bone||Sphenoid bone||Vomer||Maxilla||Palatine bone||Lacrimal bone||Inferior nasal concha

entries.name: Nasal septum
entries.description: Flat, midline structure that divides the nasal cavity into halves, formed by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone, vomer bone, and septal cartilage.

entries.name: Nasolacrimal canal
entries.description: The bony passage descends from the lacrimal-sac region of the medial orbit toward the nasal cavity behind the inferior nasal concha.

entries.name: Occipital condyles
entries.description: Paired, oval-shaped bony knobs located on the inferior skull, to either side of the foramen magnum.

entries.name: Olfactory foramina
entries.description: Numerous small openings in the ethmoid cribriform plates transmit olfactory nerve branches from the nasal cavity toward the brain.

existingTarget.name: Cribriform plate
existingTarget.relationship: related parent plate; individual foramina are separate openings

entries.name: Optic canal
entries.description: Opening spanning between middle cranial fossa and posterior orbit.

entries.name: Orbit
entries.description: Bony socket that contains the eyeball and associated muscles.
entries.pattern: Frontal bone||Sphenoid bone||Zygomatic bone||Maxilla||Palatine bone||Lacrimal bone||Ethmoid bone

entries.name: Palatine process of maxilla
entries.description: Medial projection from the maxilla bone that forms the anterior three quarters of the hard palate.

entries.name: Paranasal sinuses
entries.description: Air-filled spaces within the frontal, maxillary, ethmoid and sphenoid bones communicate with the nasal cavity.

entries.name: Perpendicular plate of ethmoid
aliases: perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone
entries.description: Downward, midline extension of the ethmoid bone that forms the superior portion of the nasal septum.

sources.term: perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone

entries.name: Petrous portion of temporal bone
entries.description: The dense temporal region forms the petrous ridge and surrounds middle- and inner-ear spaces.

entries.name: Petrous ridge
entries.description: Petrous portion of the temporal bone that forms a large, triangular ridge in the floor of the cranial cavity, separating the middle and posterior cranial fossae; houses the middle and inner ear structures.

entries.name: Posterior cranial fossa
entries.description: Deepest and most posterior cranial fossa; extends from the petrous ridge to the occipital bone.

entries.name: Posterior fontanelle
entries.description: An infant skull fibrous gap between the adjacent developing bones; locate it on a newborn specimen, not as a hole in an adult skull.
reviewNotes: Developmental feature; use the newborn-skull illustration.

entries.name: Pterion
entries.description: H-shaped suture junction region that unites the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones on the lateral side of the skull.

entries.name: Ramus of mandible
entries.description: Vertical portion of the mandible.

entries.name: Sagittal suture
entries.description: Joint that unites the right and left parietal bones at the midline along the top of the skull.

entries.name: Sella turcica
entries.description: A saddle-shaped region on the superior sphenoid body surrounds the smaller hypophyseal fossa.

entries.name: Sphenoid sinus
entries.description: Air-filled space located within the sphenoid bone; most posterior of the paranasal sinuses.

entries.name: Sphenoidal fontanelle
entries.description: An infant skull fibrous gap between the adjacent developing bones; locate it on a newborn specimen, not as a hole in an adult skull.
reviewNotes: Developmental feature; use the newborn-skull illustration.

entries.name: Squamous portion of temporal bone
entries.description: The flattened upper temporal region forms part of the lateral brain case.

entries.name: Squamous suture
entries.description: Joint that unites the parietal bone to the squamous portion of the temporal bone on the lateral side of the skull.

entries.name: Styloid process of temporal bone
entries.description: Downward projecting, elongated bony process located on the inferior aspect of the skull.

entries.name: Stylomastoid foramen
entries.description: Opening located on inferior skull, between the styloid process and mastoid process.

entries.name: Superior nasal concha
entries.description: Smallest and most superiorly located of the nasal conchae; formed by the ethmoid bone.

existingTarget.name: Superior and middle nasal conchae
existingTarget.relationship: grouped target; superior and middle conchae remain distinct

entries.name: Superior nuchal line
entries.description: Paired bony lines on the posterior skull that extend laterally from the external occipital protuberance.

entries.name: Superior orbital fissure
entries.description: An irregular opening between the greater and lesser sphenoid wings connects the middle cranial fossa with the posterior orbit.

entries.name: Supraorbital foramen
entries.description: Opening located on anterior skull, at the superior margin of the orbit.

entries.name: Supraorbital margin
entries.description: Superior margin of the orbit.

entries.name: Temporal fossa
entries.description: Shallow space on the lateral side of the skull, above the level of the zygomatic arch.
entries.pattern: Frontal bone||Parietal bone||Temporal bone||Sphenoid bone||Zygomatic bone

entries.name: Temporal process of the zygomatic bone
entries.description: Short extension from the zygomatic bone that forms the anterior portion of the zygomatic arch.

sources.term: temporal process of the zygomatic bone

entries.name: Zygomatic arch
entries.description: Elongated, free-standing arch on the lateral skull, formed anteriorly by the temporal process of the zygomatic bone and posteriorly by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone.

entries.name: Zygomatic process of maxilla
entries.description: The lateral maxillary projection toward the zygomatic bone is labeled in the isolated maxilla illustration.
reviewNotes: Figure shows this process cut; a cut end must not be mistaken for a natural opening.

entries.name: Zygomatic process of the temporal bone
entries.description: Extension from the temporal bone that forms the posterior portion of the zygomatic arch.

sources.term: zygomatic process of the temporal bone

entries.name: Anterior arch of atlas
entries.description: Anterior portion of the ring-like C1 (atlas) vertebra.

entries.name: Anterior sacral foramina
entries.description: One of the series of paired openings located on the anterior (ventral) side of the sacrum.

existingTarget.name: Sacral foramina
existingTarget.relationship: grouped target; anterior and posterior foramina require distinct views

entries.name: Apex of sacrum
entries.description: The inferior tapered end of the sacrum meets the coccyx.

entries.name: Auricular surface of sacrum
entries.description: The rough lateral sacral articular surface joins the matching auricular surface of the ilium at the sacroiliac joint.

entries.name: Base of sacrum
entries.description: The broad superior sacral region receives weight from L5 and narrows inferiorly toward the apex.

entries.name: Bifid spinous process
entries.description: The split tip of a typical cervical spinous process is illustrated as a cervical identifying feature.
reviewNotes: C1 lacks a spinous process and C7 usually has a prominent nonbifid process; the typical illustration is not every cervical level.

entries.name: Body of first sacral vertebra
entries.description: The superior central weight-bearing sacral body is the fused remnant of S1.

entries.name: Costal facets
entries.description: Articular surfaces on thoracic vertebral bodies receive rib heads; a separate transverse-process facet receives the rib tubercle.

entries.name: Dens
entries.description: Bony projection (odontoid process) that extends upward from the body of the C2 (axis) vertebra.

entries.name: Inferior articular facets
entries.description: The smooth joint surfaces on the inferior articular processes meet the superior facets of the vertebra below.
reviewNotes: Facet is the articular surface; process is the projection carrying it.

entries.name: Inferior articular process
entries.description: Bony process that extends downward from the vertebral arch of a vertebra that articulates with the superior articular process of the next lower vertebra.

entries.name: Inferior costal facet
entries.description: The inferior rib-head articular surface on a typical thoracic vertebral body meets part of the next rib head.
reviewNotes: Typical pattern varies at upper and lower thoracic levels.

entries.name: Intervertebral foramen
entries.description: Opening located between adjacent vertebrae for exit of a spinal nerve.

entries.name: Lamina
entries.description: Portion of the vertebral arch on each vertebra that extends between the transverse and spinous process.

entries.name: Lateral sacral crest
entries.description: A paired ridge on the posterior sacrum reflects fusion of the sacral transverse processes.

entries.name: Median sacral crest
entries.description: Irregular ridge running down the midline of the posterior sacrum that was formed from the fusion of the spinous processes of the five sacral vertebrae.

entries.name: Pedicles
entries.description: Portion of the vertebral arch that extends from the vertebral body to the transverse process.

entries.name: Posterior arch of atlas
entries.description: Posterior portion of the ring-like C1 (atlas) vertebra.

entries.name: Posterior sacral foramina
entries.description: One of the series of paired openings located on the posterior (dorsal) side of the sacrum.

existingTarget.name: Sacral foramina
existingTarget.relationship: grouped target; anterior and posterior foramina require distinct views

entries.name: Sacral canal
entries.description: Bony tunnel that runs through the sacrum.

entries.name: Sacral foramina
entries.description: Series of paired openings for nerve exit located on both the anterior (ventral) and posterior (dorsal) aspects of the sacrum.

entries.name: Sacral hiatus
entries.description: Inferior opening and termination of the sacral canal.

entries.name: Sacral promontory
entries.description: Anterior lip of the base (superior end) of the sacrum.

entries.name: Spinous process
entries.description: Unpaired bony process that extends posteriorly from the vertebral arch of a vertebra.

entries.name: Superior articular facet of sacrum
entries.description: The articular surface of a superior sacral process meets the inferior articular facet of L5.
reviewNotes: Do not merge the surface with the entire superior articular process.

entries.name: Superior articular facets
entries.description: The smooth joint surfaces on the superior articular processes meet the inferior facets of the vertebra above.
reviewNotes: Facet is the articular surface; process is the projection carrying it.

entries.name: Superior articular process
entries.description: Bony process that extends upward from the vertebral arch of a vertebra that articulates with the inferior articular process of the next higher vertebra.

entries.name: Superior articular process of the sacrum
entries.description: Paired processes that extend upward from the sacrum to articulate (join) with the inferior articular processes from the L5 vertebra.

sources.term: superior articular process of the sacrum

entries.name: Superior costal facet
entries.description: The superior rib-head articular surface on a thoracic vertebral body participates in the joint with a rib head.
reviewNotes: Typical pattern varies with vertebral level; do not place the same pair on every thoracic vertebra.

entries.name: Transverse costal facet
entries.description: The rib-tubercle joint surface lies on a thoracic transverse process, distinct from rib-head facets on the body.
reviewNotes: Absent on the lower floating-rib levels; do not duplicate across every thoracic vertebra.

entries.name: Transverse foramen
entries.description: Opening found only in the transverse processes of cervical vertebrae.

entries.name: Transverse process
entries.description: Paired bony processes that extends laterally from the vertebral arch of a vertebra.

entries.name: Transverse sacral ridges
entries.description: Four transverse ridges on the anterior adult sacrum mark the fusion lines between sacral vertebral bodies.

entries.name: Vertebral arch
entries.description: Bony arch formed by the posterior portion of each vertebra that surrounds and protects the spinal cord.

entries.name: Vertebral body
entries.description: The anterior weight-bearing portion of a typical vertebra lies in front of the vertebral foramen.

entries.name: Vertebral canal
entries.description: The continuous passage formed by the aligned vertebral foramina houses the spinal cord and its coverings.

entries.name: Vertebral foramen
entries.description: The opening enclosed by one vertebral body and vertebral arch contributes to the continuous vertebral canal when the vertebrae are articulated.

existingTarget.name: Vertebral canal
existingTarget.relationship: related; one vertebral opening contributes to the continuous canal

entries.name: Angle of rib
entries.description: Portion of rib with greatest curvature; together, the rib angles form the most posterior extent of the thoracic cage.

entries.name: Body of hyoid
entries.description: The central part of the U-shaped hyoid lies anterior to its projecting horns.

sources.kind: Figure 7.19 labels, anterior and lateral views

reviewNotes: Hyoid lies in the neck and is not a skull bone; the existing atlas groups it with thoracic/neck context.

entries.name: Body of rib
entries.description: Shaft portion of a rib.

entries.name: Body of sternum
entries.description: The elongated middle sternum lies below the manubrium and above the xiphoid process.

entries.name: Clavicular notch
entries.description: Paired notches located on the superior-lateral sides of the sternal manubrium, for articulation with the clavicle.

entries.name: Costal groove
entries.description: Shallow groove along the inferior margin of a rib that provides passage for blood vessels and a nerve.

entries.name: Greater horn of hyoid
entries.description: The longer paired hyoid horns project posteriorly from the body.

sources.kind: Figure 7.19 labels, anterior and lateral views

entries.name: Head of rib
entries.description: Posterior end of a rib that articulates with the bodies of thoracic vertebrae.

entries.name: Jugular notch
entries.description: Shallow notch located on superior surface of sternal manubrium.

entries.name: Lesser horn of hyoid
entries.description: The shorter paired hyoid projections arise near the junction of the body and greater horns.

sources.kind: Figure 7.19 labels, anterior and lateral views

entries.name: Manubrium
entries.description: The broad superior sternum bears the jugular and clavicular notches.

entries.name: Neck of rib
entries.description: Narrowed region of a rib, next to the rib head.

entries.name: Sternal angle
entries.description: Junction line between manubrium and body of the sternum and the site for attachment of the second rib to the sternum.

entries.name: Tubercle of rib
entries.description: Small bump on the posterior side of a rib for articulation with the transverse process of a thoracic vertebra.

entries.name: Xiphoid process
entries.description: Small process that forms the inferior tip of the sternum.

entries.name: Suture
entries.description: A fibrous joint between adjacent skull bones, represented by its junction line.
reviewNotes: Generic marking vocabulary, not an additional named skeletal instance.

entries.name: Adductor tubercle
entries.description: Small, bony bump located on the superior aspect of the medial epicondyle of the femur.

entries.name: Anterior border of the tibia
entries.description: Narrow, anterior margin of the tibia that extends inferiorly from the tibial tuberosity.

entries.name: Articular surface of lateral tibial condyle
aliases: Articular surface of the lateral tibial condyle
entries.description: The smooth superior surface of the lateral tibial condyle contributes to the tibiofemoral joint.

sources.term: Articular surface of lateral tibial condyle

reviewNotes: The articular surface is a subfeature of the whole lateral condyle.

entries.name: Articular surface of medial tibial condyle
aliases: Articular surface of the medial tibial condyle
entries.description: The smooth superior surface of the medial tibial condyle contributes to the tibiofemoral joint.

sources.term: Articular surface of medial tibial condyle

reviewNotes: The articular surface is a subfeature of the whole medial condyle.

entries.name: Base of fifth metatarsal
entries.description: The expanded proximal fifth-metatarsal region projects along the lateral foot and provides muscle attachment.

sources.kind: Figure 8.19 superior view and body PDF322

reviewNotes: The tuberosity projects from this base; do not equate the whole base with only its tuberosity.

entries.name: Base of the metatarsal bone
entries.description: Expanded, proximal end of each metatarsal bone.

entries.name: Calcaneal tuberosity
entries.description: The broad posterior-inferior calcaneal prominence forms the bony heel.

entries.name: Facet for medial malleolus
entries.description: The smooth medial talar surface articulates with the medial malleolus of the tibia.

entries.name: Fibular notch of tibia
entries.description: A depression on the lateral distal tibia articulates with the distal fibula; it is a feature of the tibia.

entries.name: Fovea capitis
entries.description: Minor indentation on the head of the femur that serves as the site of attachment for the ligament to the head of the femur.

entries.name: Gluteal tuberosity
entries.description: Roughened area on the posterior side of the proximal femur, extending inferiorly from the base of the greater trochanter.

entries.name: Greater trochanter
entries.description: Large, bony expansion of the femur that projects superiorly from the base of the femoral neck.

entries.name: Head of the femur
entries.description: Rounded, proximal end of the femur that articulates with the acetabulum of the hip bone to form the hip joint.

entries.name: Head of the fibula
entries.description: Small, knob-like, proximal end of the fibula; articulates with the inferior aspect of the lateral condyle of the tibia.

entries.name: Head of the metatarsal bone
entries.description: Expanded, distal end of each metatarsal bone.

entries.name: Inferior articular surface of tibia
aliases: Inferior articular surface of the tibia
entries.description: The smooth distal tibial surface articulates with the superior talar surface at the ankle.

entries.name: Inferior tendon groove of cuboid
aliases: Groove for fibularis longus tendon of cuboid
Groove for peroneus longus tendon of cuboid
entries.description: The deep groove across the inferior cuboid surface provides a tendon passage. The supplied text describes this feature without a proper name.

sources.kind: Body text beginning PDF321 and continuing PDF322

reviewNotes: Source-guide entry: the standard tendon identity comes from FIPAT TA2 item1490, while OpenStax describes an unnamed tendon groove. The source foot figure does not expose the inferior cuboid surface; do not place a guessed target on a superior/medial view.
Use source description and an orientation guide unless a separate inferior-surface view is independently verified.

externalSources.title: FIPAT Terminologia Anatomica 2, Part II, item1490

entries.name: Intercondylar eminence of tibia
entries.description: Irregular elevation on the superior end of the tibia, between the articulating surfaces of the medial and lateral condyles.

entries.name: Intercondylar fossa of femur
entries.description: Deep depression on the posterior side of the distal femur that separates the medial and lateral condyles.

entries.name: Interosseous border of the fibula
entries.description: Small ridge running down the medial side of the fibular shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the fibula and tibia.

entries.name: Interosseous border of the tibia
entries.description: Small ridge running down the lateral side of the tibial shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the tibia and fibula.

entries.name: Intertrochanteric crest
entries.description: Short, prominent ridge running between the greater and lesser trochanters on the posterior side of the proximal femur.

entries.name: Intertrochanteric line
entries.description: Small ridge running between the greater and lesser trochanters on the anterior side of the proximal femur.

entries.name: Lateral condyle of the femur
entries.description: Smooth, articulating surface that forms the distal and posterior sides of the lateral expansion of the distal femur.

entries.name: Lateral condyle of the tibia
entries.description: Lateral, expanded region of the proximal tibia that includes the smooth surface that articulates with the lateral condyle of the femur as part of the knee joint.

entries.name: Lateral epicondyle of the femur
entries.description: Roughened area of the femur located on the lateral side of the lateral condyle.

entries.name: Lateral longitudinal arch of foot
entries.description: The lower, flatter longitudinal foot arch runs along the lateral foot.

entries.name: Lateral malleolus
entries.description: Expanded distal end of the fibula.

entries.name: Lesser trochanter
entries.description: Small, bony projection on the medial side of the proximal femur, at the base of the femoral neck.

entries.name: Linea aspera
entries.description: Longitudinally running bony ridge located in the middle third of the posterior femur.

entries.name: Medial condyle of the femur
entries.description: Smooth, articulating surface that forms the distal and posterior sides of the medial expansion of the distal femur.

entries.name: Medial condyle of the tibia
entries.description: Medial, expanded region of the proximal tibia that includes the smooth surface that articulates with the medial condyle of the femur as part of the knee joint.

entries.name: Medial epicondyle of the femur
entries.description: Roughened area of the distal femur located on the medial side of the medial condyle.

entries.name: Medial longitudinal arch of foot
entries.description: The taller longitudinal foot arch runs along the medial foot and supports spring and shock absorption.
reviewNotes: Use the composite foot diagram rather than a pin on one tarsal bone.

entries.name: Medial malleolus
entries.description: Bony expansion located on the medial side of the distal tibia.

entries.name: Neck of the femur
entries.description: Narrowed region located inferior to the head of the femur.

entries.name: Patellar surface
entries.description: Smooth groove located on the anterior side of the distal femur, between the medial and lateral condyles; site of articulation for the patella.

entries.name: Shaft of metatarsal bone
entries.description: The elongated central part of a metatarsal lies between its base and head.

entries.name: Shaft of the femur
entries.description: Cylindrically shaped region that forms the central portion of the femur.

entries.name: Shaft of the fibula
entries.description: Elongated, slender portion located between the expanded ends of the fibula.

entries.name: Shaft of the tibia
entries.description: Triangular-shaped, central portion of the tibia.

entries.name: Soleal line
entries.description: Small, diagonally running ridge located on the posterior side of the proximal tibia.

entries.name: Sustentaculum tali
entries.description: Bony ledge extending from the medial side of the calcaneus bone.

entries.name: Tibial tuberosity
entries.description: Elevated area on the anterior surface of the proximal tibia.

entries.name: Transverse arch of foot
entries.description: The side-to-side midfoot arch is formed by wedge-shaped cuneiforms and the proximal first through fourth metatarsals.

entries.name: Trochlea of talus
entries.description: The superior pulley-shaped articular surface of the talus fits against the distal tibia at the ankle.
reviewNotes: Distinct from the trochlea of the humerus and the soft-tissue orbital trochlea.

entries.name: Acetabulum
entries.description: Large, cup-shaped cavity located on the lateral side of the hip bone; formed by the junction of the ilium, pubis, and ischium portions of the hip bone.

entries.name: Anterior inferior iliac spine
entries.description: Small, bony projection located on the anterior margin of the ilium, below the anterior superior iliac spine.

entries.name: Anterior superior iliac spine
entries.description: Rounded, anterior end of the iliac crest.

entries.name: Arcuate line of the ilium
entries.description: Smooth ridge located at the inferior margin of the iliac fossa; forms the lateral portion of the pelvic brim.

entries.name: Auricular surface of the ilium
entries.description: Roughened area located on the posterior, medial side of the ilium of the hip bone; articulates with the auricular surface of the sacrum to form the sacroiliac joint.

entries.name: Greater pelvis
entries.description: The broad pelvic space superior to the pelvic brim is bounded laterally by the upper ilia.

entries.name: Greater sciatic foramen
entries.description: The greater sciatic notch is completed into a passage by the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments; the bony notch alone is not the complete foramen.
reviewNotes: Requires contributing ligaments and hip bone together; do not confuse the bony notch with the completed foramen.

entries.name: Greater sciatic notch
entries.description: Large, U-shaped indentation located on the posterior margin of the ilium, superior to the ischial spine.

entries.name: Iliac crest
entries.description: Curved, superior margin of the ilium.

entries.name: Iliac fossa
entries.description: Shallow depression found on the anterior and medial surfaces of the upper ilium.

entries.name: Inferior pubic ramus
entries.description: Narrow segment of bone that passes inferiorly and laterally from the pubic body; joins with the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus.

entries.name: Ischial ramus
entries.description: Bony extension projecting anteriorly and superiorly from the ischial tuberosity; joins with the inferior pubic ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus.

entries.name: Ischial spine
entries.description: Pointed, bony projection from the posterior margin of the ischium that separates the greater sciatic notch and lesser sciatic notch.

entries.name: Ischial tuberosity
entries.description: Large, roughened protuberance that forms the posteroinferior portion of the hip bone; weight-bearing region of the pelvis when sitting.

entries.name: Ischiopubic ramus
entries.description: Narrow extension of bone that connects the ischial tuberosity to the pubic body; formed by the junction of the ischial ramus and inferior pubic ramus.

entries.name: Lesser pelvis
entries.description: The narrower true pelvic space lies between the pelvic inlet and pelvic outlet.

entries.name: Lesser sciatic foramen
entries.description: The lesser sciatic notch and the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments bound this passage below the ischial spine.
reviewNotes: Requires contributing ligaments and hip bone together; do not confuse the bony notch with the completed foramen.

entries.name: Lesser sciatic notch
entries.description: Shallow indentation along the posterior margin of the ischium, inferior to the ischial spine.

entries.name: Obturator foramen
entries.description: Large opening located in the anterior hip bone, between the pubis and ischium regions.

entries.name: Pectineal line of pubis
entries.description: Narrow ridge located on the superior surface of the superior pubic ramus.

entries.name: Pelvic brim
entries.description: The inlet margin separates the greater and lesser pelvis and follows the upper pubic symphysis, pectineal lines, arcuate lines and sacral promontory.

entries.name: Pelvic outlet
entries.description: The inferior opening of the lesser pelvis is bounded by the lower pubic symphysis, ischiopubic rami, sacrotuberous ligaments and coccygeal tip.
reviewNotes: Ligaments are part of the complete boundary.

entries.name: Posterior inferior iliac spine
entries.description: Small, bony projection located at the inferior margin of the auricular surface on the posterior ilium.

entries.name: Posterior superior iliac spine
entries.description: Rounded, posterior end of the iliac crest.

entries.name: Pubic arch
entries.description: Bony structure formed by the pubic symphysis, and the bodies and inferior pubic rami of the right and left pubic bones.

entries.name: Pubic body
entries.description: Enlarged, medial portion of the pubis region of the hip bone.

entries.name: Pubic tubercle
entries.description: Small bump located on the superior aspect of the pubic body.

entries.name: Subpubic angle
entries.description: Inverted V-shape formed by the convergence of the right and left ischiopubic rami; this angle is greater than 80 degrees in females and less than 70 degrees in males.

entries.name: Superior pubic ramus
entries.description: Narrow segment of bone that passes laterally from the pubic body to join the ilium.

entries.name: Symphyseal surface of pubis
entries.description: The medial articular surface of the pubic body meets the pubic symphysis.

entries.name: Acromial end of the clavicle
entries.description: Lateral end of the clavicle that articulates with the acromion of the scapula.

entries.name: Acromion
entries.description: Acromion of the scapula.
reviewNotes: Alias normalization required: acromial process = acromion; bicipital groove = intertubercular groove. These are source rows, not extra unique structures.
Canonical alias merge prevents double-counting one structure as two landmarks.

entries.name: Anatomical neck of humerus
entries.description: Line on the humerus located around the outside margin of the humeral head.

entries.name: Base of metacarpal bone
entries.description: The proximal metacarpal end articulates with the distal carpal row.

entries.name: Base of proximal phalanx of hand
aliases: Base of the proximal phalanx of the hand
entries.description: The proximal end of a proximal finger phalanx articulates with a metacarpal head.

sources.term: Base of proximal phalanx of hand

entries.name: Capitulum
entries.description: Knob-like bony structure located anteriorly on the lateral, distal end of the humerus.

entries.name: Carpal tunnel
entries.description: The U-shaped carpal bones form the floor and walls of a passage roofed by the flexor retinaculum.
reviewNotes: Requires flexor-retinaculum context; a bony groove alone is not the complete tunnel.

entries.name: Coracoid process
entries.description: Short, hook-like process that projects anteriorly and laterally from the superior margin of the scapula.

entries.name: Coronoid fossa
entries.description: Depression on the anterior surface of the humerus above the trochlea; this space receives the coronoid process of the ulna when the elbow is maximally flexed.

entries.name: Coronoid process of the ulna
entries.description: Projecting bony lip located on the anterior, proximal ulna; forms the inferior margin of the trochlear notch.

entries.name: Deltoid tuberosity
entries.description: Roughened, V-shaped region located laterally on the mid-shaft of the humerus.

entries.name: Glenoid cavity
entries.description: (also, glenoid fossa) shallow depression located on the lateral scapula, between the superior and lateral borders.

entries.name: Greater tubercle
entries.description: Enlarged prominence located on the lateral side of the proximal humerus.

entries.name: Head of metacarpal bone
entries.description: The expanded distal metacarpal end forms a knuckle and articulates with the base of a proximal phalanx.

entries.name: Head of proximal phalanx of hand
aliases: Head of the proximal phalanx of the hand
entries.description: The expanded distal end of a proximal finger phalanx participates in the proximal interphalangeal joint.

sources.term: Head of proximal phalanx of hand

reviewNotes: The figure identifies the feature on one illustrated finger; do not treat a point as the outline of the whole articular head.

entries.name: Head of the humerus
entries.description: Smooth, rounded region on the medial side of the proximal humerus; articulates with the glenoid fossa of the scapula to form the glenohumeral (shoulder) joint.

entries.name: Head of the radius
entries.description: Disc-shaped structure that forms the proximal end of the radius; articulates with the capitulum of the humerus as part of the elbow joint, and with the radial notch of the ulna as part of the proximal radioulnar joint.

entries.name: Head of the ulna
entries.description: Small, rounded distal end of the ulna; articulates with the ulnar notch of the distal radius, forming the distal radioulnar joint.

entries.name: Hook of hamate
entries.description: Bony extension located on the anterior side of the hamate carpal bone.

entries.name: Inferior angle of the scapula
entries.description: Inferior corner of the scapula located where the medial and lateral borders meet.

entries.name: Infraglenoid tubercle
entries.description: Small bump or roughened area located on the lateral border of the scapula, near the inferior margin of the glenoid cavity.

entries.name: Infraspinous fossa
entries.description: Broad depression located on the posterior scapula, inferior to the spine.

entries.name: Interosseous border of the radius
entries.description: Narrow ridge located on the medial side of the radial shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the ulna and radius bones.

entries.name: Interosseous border of the ulna
entries.description: Narrow ridge located on the lateral side of the ulnar shaft; for attachment of the interosseous membrane between the ulna and radius.

entries.name: Intertubercular groove of humerus
entries.description: The narrow groove between the greater and lesser humeral tubercles is also called the bicipital groove.
reviewNotes: Alias normalization required: acromial process = acromion; bicipital groove = intertubercular groove. These are source rows, not extra unique structures.
Canonical alias merge prevents double-counting one structure as two landmarks.

entries.name: Lateral border of the scapula
entries.description: Diagonally oriented lateral margin of the scapula.

entries.name: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
entries.description: Small projection located on the lateral side of the distal humerus.

entries.name: Lateral supracondylar ridge
entries.description: Narrow, bony ridge located along the lateral side of the distal humerus, superior to the lateral epicondyle.

entries.name: Lesser tubercle
entries.description: Small, bony prominence located on anterior side of the proximal humerus.

entries.name: Medial border of the scapula
entries.description: Elongated, medial margin of the scapula.

entries.name: Medial epicondyle of the humerus
entries.description: Enlarged projection located on the medial side of the distal humerus.

entries.name: Neck of the radius
entries.description: Narrowed region immediately distal to the head of the radius.

entries.name: Olecranon
entries.description: Expanded posterior and superior portions of the proximal ulna; forms the bony tip of the elbow.

entries.name: Olecranon fossa
entries.description: Large depression located on the posterior side of the distal humerus; this space receives the olecranon process of the ulna when the elbow is fully extended.

entries.name: Radial fossa
entries.description: Small depression located on the anterior humerus above the capitulum; this space receives the head of the radius when the elbow is maximally flexed.

entries.name: Radial notch of the ulna
entries.description: Small, smooth area on the lateral side of the proximal ulna; articulates with the head of the radius as part of the proximal radioulnar joint.

entries.name: Radial tuberosity
entries.description: Oval-shaped, roughened protuberance located on the medial side of the proximal radius.

entries.name: Scapular spine
entries.description: Prominent ridge passing mediolaterally across the upper portion of the posterior scapular surface.

entries.name: Shaft of clavicle
entries.description: The curved central clavicle lies between its medial sternal end and lateral acromial end.

entries.name: Shaft of metacarpal bone
entries.description: The central portion of a metacarpal lies between the proximal base and distal head.

entries.name: Shaft of proximal phalanx of hand
aliases: Shaft of the proximal phalanx of the hand
entries.description: The central portion of a proximal finger phalanx lies between its base and head.

sources.term: Shaft of proximal phalanx of hand

entries.name: Shaft of the humerus
entries.description: Narrow, elongated, central region of the humerus.

entries.name: Shaft of the radius
entries.description: Narrow, elongated, central region of the radius.

entries.name: Shaft of the ulna
entries.description: Narrow, elongated, central region of the ulna.

entries.name: Sternal end of the clavicle
entries.description: Medial end of the clavicle that articulates with the manubrium of the sternum.

entries.name: Styloid process of the radius
entries.description: Pointed projection located on the lateral end of the distal radius.

entries.name: Styloid process of the ulna
entries.description: Short, bony projection located on the medial end of the distal ulna.

entries.name: Subscapular fossa
entries.description: Broad depression located on the anterior (deep) surface of the scapula.

entries.name: Superior angle of the scapula
entries.description: Corner of the scapula between the superior and medial borders of the scapula.

entries.name: Superior border of the scapula
entries.description: Superior margin of the scapula.

entries.name: Supraglenoid tubercle
entries.description: Small bump located at the superior margin of the glenoid cavity.

entries.name: Suprascapular notch
entries.description: Small notch located along the superior border of the scapula, medial to the coracoid process.

entries.name: Supraspinous fossa
entries.description: Narrow depression located on the posterior scapula, superior to the spine.

entries.name: Surgical neck of humerus
entries.description: The region where the expanded proximal humerus meets the narrower shaft lies distal to the tubercles.

entries.name: Trochlea
entries.description: Pulley-shaped region located medially at the distal end of the humerus; articulates at the elbow with the trochlear notch of the ulna.

entries.name: Trochlear notch
entries.description: Large, C-shaped depression located on the anterior side of the proximal ulna; articulates at the elbow with the trochlea of the humerus.

entries.name: Ulnar notch of the radius
entries.description: Shallow, smooth area located on the medial side of the distal radius; articulates with the head of the ulna at the distal radioulnar joint.

entries.name: Ulnar tuberosity
entries.description: Roughened area located on the anterior, proximal ulna inferior to the coronoid process.

entries.name: Pubic crest
entries.description: The superior border of the pubic body, near the symphysis, is named as an origin of rectus abdominis in the muscle chapter.

entries.name: Pterygoid process of sphenoid
entries.description: The inferior sphenoid projection includes the medial and lateral pterygoid plates; it is named as an attachment in the chewing-muscle table.

entries.name: Anterior semicircular canal
entries.description: One of the two approximately vertical semicircular bony canals is oriented at about 45 degrees to the sagittal plane; its sensory duct responds to rotation in its plane.
reviewNotes: The text names anterior and posterior vertical canals; the diagram introduces their arrangement. Do not confuse the bony canal with the sensory membranous duct inside it.
Use source guide unless a distinct canal target is visually verified; no unvalidated adult surface pin.

entries.name: Bony labyrinth
entries.description: The interconnected osseous spaces of the inner ear lie inside the temporal bone and contain the membranous labyrinth.
reviewNotes: Whole-book extension. Separate osseous spaces from membranous ducts and sensory tissues; current skeleton cannot be assumed to contain usable geometry.

entries.name: Cochlea
entries.description: The coiled osseous region of the inner ear surrounds the hearing apparatus within the temporal bone.
reviewNotes: The cochlear duct and organ of Corti are soft tissues; do not call them bone.

entries.name: Lateral semicircular canal
entries.description: The approximately horizontal semicircular bony canal is oriented differently from the anterior and posterior vertical canals.
reviewNotes: OpenStax describes one canal in the horizontal plane; lateral is the standardized anatomical name used for this canal.
Use source guide unless a distinct canal target is visually verified; no unvalidated adult surface pin.

entries.name: Oval window
entries.description: The oval opening between middle ear and vestibular region is occupied by the stapes footplate and transmits vibration into the inner ear.
reviewNotes: Show a labeled ear cutaway; a closed outer temporal mesh cannot expose the window.

entries.name: Posterior semicircular canal
entries.description: The posterior member of the approximately vertical semicircular canal pair lies in a plane about 45 degrees from the sagittal plane.
reviewNotes: Distinguish the bony canal from its enclosed sensory duct.
Use source guide unless a distinct canal target is visually verified; no unvalidated adult surface pin.

entries.name: Round window
entries.description: The membrane-covered opening at the cochlear base marks the end of the scala tympani.
reviewNotes: Distinguish the bony opening from its covering membrane.

entries.name: Semicircular canals
entries.description: Three curved osseous canals extend from the vestibular region of each temporal bone; distinguish the bony canals from the sensory ducts inside them.
reviewNotes: Whole-book extension. Separate osseous spaces from membranous ducts and sensory tissues; current skeleton cannot be assumed to contain usable geometry.

entries.name: Vestibule of inner ear
entries.description: The central vestibular osseous region of the bony labyrinth connects with the semicircular canals and cochlear region.
reviewNotes: Utricle and saccule are membranous structures inside it.
